metadata.title: Policy alignment questionnaire
metadata.basis: Thematic summaries of nine parties' 2024 general-election manifestos currently published on Irish Policy Monitor.
metadata.warning: Indicative self-assessment, not a voting recommendation. It compares broad policy direction, not every detailed proposal, current party policy, candidate record, coalition likelihood or implementation performance. Party positions may be incomplete or change.

dimensions.label: Housing
dimensions.question: Which approach is closest to your view?

options.label: The State should directly build much more social and affordable housing and strengthen renter protections.
Increase supply through a mix of public, affordable and private construction, planning reform and infrastructure.
Prioritise private construction, incentives for buyers and landlords, and faster planning to expand supply.
I am unsure / none of these fully reflects my view.

dimensions.label: Health
dimensions.question: What should be the main direction for healthcare?

options.label: Expand universal public provision, reduce reliance on private care and invest strongly in public capacity.
Improve public access and capacity through reform, workforce expansion and a mix of delivery approaches.
Increase choice and capacity using public, private and community providers.
I am unsure / none of these fully reflects my view.

dimensions.label: Economy and taxation
dimensions.question: Which economic and tax approach do you favour?

options.label: More progressive taxation and stronger public services and social protection.
A balanced approach: support enterprise and jobs while funding public services and targeted supports.
Lower tax burdens, competitiveness, private enterprise and incentives for investment.
I am unsure / none of these fully reflects my view.

dimensions.label: Climate and energy
dimensions.question: How should Ireland pursue climate and energy goals?

options.label: Accelerate emissions cuts and public investment, with a strong just-transition and household protections.
Continue climate action while balancing affordability, energy security and effects on farms and businesses.
Slow or reconsider targets where costs, energy security or economic impacts are too high.
I am unsure / none of these fully reflects my view.

dimensions.label: Immigration and asylum
dimensions.question: Which approach is closest to your view?

options.label: Emphasise humanitarian obligations, rights, integration and fair procedures.
Combine fair procedures and integration with efficient processing and managed migration.
Prioritise tighter controls, faster decisions, enforcement and reduced irregular migration.
I am unsure / none of these fully reflects my view.
Reduce costs for families and expand inclusive, special-needs and early-years provision.
Improve school places, teacher capacity, skills, apprenticeships and childcare.
Increase parental choice, flexibility and diverse education options.
I am unsure / none of these fully reflects my view.

scoring: For each answered issue, an exact broad-category match receives 2 points and an adjacent/overlapping match receives 1 point where editorially defined; unmatched or unsure answers receive 0. Issue weights are shown. Scores are an approximate fit indicator, not probabilities or endorsements.
